_comment: Data batch 2026-10b, applied by scripts/add-data-batch-2026-10b.mjs. Facts (coordinates, dates, Q-ids, sitelinks as notability) were read from Wikidata on 21 Oct 2026; summaries, sides and results were written by hand from the English Wikipedia article named in sourceUrl. Discoveries cite the peer-reviewed paper. 'country' is used only by the test that checks each pin lands in the right country; the script does not copy it into events.json.

battles.name: Battle of Amoaful
battles.summary: Sir Garnet Wolseley's British force beat the Asante army in thick forest on its march to Kumasi, in the Third Anglo-Ashanti War.

battles.name: Battle of Sidi Brahim
battles.summary: Emir Abdelkader's horsemen destroyed a French column near Sidi Brahim in western Algeria; a few survivors held out in a shrine for days.
battles.dateNote: Fought over three days, 23 to 25 September 1845.

battles.name: Battle of Italeni
battles.summary: A Voortrekker commando led by Piet Uys and Hendrik Potgieter rode into a Zulu ambush; Uys and his young son were killed.

battles.name: Battle of Boomplaats
battles.summary: Sir Harry Smith's British force defeated Andries Pretorius's Boers, keeping the Orange River Sovereignty under British rule for a few more years.

battles.name: Siege of Eshowe
battles.summary: Colonel Charles Pearson's British column was hemmed in at the Eshowe mission station by Zulu forces for about ten weeks, until it was relieved in April 1879.
battles.dateNote: The siege lasted from late January to early April 1879.

battles.name: Battle of Embabo
battles.summary: Menelik of Shewa defeated and captured Tekle Haymanot of Gojjam in a fight over the rich lands to the south-west, which made Menelik the strongest ruler in Ethiopia after the emperor.

battles.name: Battle of Ginnis
battles.summary: An Anglo-Egyptian force beat a Mahdist army on the Nile in northern Sudan. It is often said to be the last battle British soldiers fought in red coats.

battles.name: Battle of Salt River
battles.summary: Khoikhoi herders by Table Bay beat a Portuguese landing party. Francisco de Almeida, the first viceroy of Portuguese India, was killed.

battles.name: Battle of Tsuntua
battles.summary: Early in the Fulani jihad the army of Gobir defeated Usman dan Fodio's followers and killed many of their scholars. The movement still went on to found the Sokoto Caliphate.
battles.dateNote: Wikidata gives the month only: December 1804.

battles.name: Battle of Logandème
battles.summary: Louis Faidherbe's French colonial troops beat the Serer army of the Kingdom of Sine near Fatick in Senegal.

battles.name: Capture of Gorée
battles.summary: A British naval squadron under Augustus Keppel took the French island trading post of Gorée, off Dakar, in the Seven Years' War.

battles.name: Battle of Barawa
battles.summary: A Portuguese fleet under Tristão da Cunha attacked and sacked the Somali port town of Barawa.
battles.dateNote: Wikidata gives the month only: April 1507.

battles.name: Battle of Porédaka
battles.summary: French troops defeated Almamy Bokar Biro, ending the independence of the Imamate of Futa Jallon in today's Guinea.

battles.name: Battle of Lukaya
battles.summary: In the Uganda–Tanzania War, Tanzanian forces beat back a Ugandan and Libyan counter-attack near Lukaya, opening the road to Kampala and the fall of Idi Amin.

battles.name: Battle of Chinsurah
battles.summary: British troops under Francis Forde beat a Dutch force near Chinsurah in Bengal, ending Dutch hopes of rivalling the British there.

battles.name: Battle of Porto Novo
battles.summary: Sir Eyre Coote's outnumbered British army defeated Hyder Ali of Mysore on the Coromandel coast, in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

battles.name: Battle of Arnee
battles.summary: Soon after his defence of Arcot, Robert Clive beat a French-backed force at Arni, in the Second Carnatic War.

battles.name: Battle of Bhangani
battles.summary: The young Guru Gobind Singh's followers beat an alliance of hill rajas near Paonta Sahib, his first battle.
sides: Hill rajas led by Bhim Chand

battles.name: Battle of Mahidpur
battles.summary: A British army defeated the Holkar army of Indore in the Third Anglo-Maratha War, breaking Holkar power.

battles.name: Battle of Hyderabad (Sindh)
battles.summary: Sir Charles Napier's army defeated the Talpur Amirs near Hyderabad, completing the British conquest of Sindh.

battles.name: Battle of Shopian
battles.summary: Ranjit Singh's Sikh army beat the Afghan governor's forces at Shopian, bringing Kashmir into the Sikh Empire.

battles.name: Sack of Surat
battles.summary: Shivaji's Maratha horsemen raided the rich Mughal port of Surat and looted it for several days.

battles.name: Battle of Manila (1570)
battles.summary: A Spanish force under Martín de Goiti attacked Rajah Sulayman's fortified town of Maynila. A year later the Spanish made Manila their capital in the Philippines.

battles.name: Battle of Sondani
battles.summary: The Indian king Yashodharman recorded on victory pillars at Sondani that he had defeated the Hun ruler Mihirakula.
battles.dateNote: The year is not known exactly; about 528 CE is the usual estimate.

battles.name: Battle of Yu Oc
battles.summary: In the Sino-French War a French column fought through a Chinese and Black Flag ambush at Yu Oc, on its way to relieve Tuyên Quang.
sides: Black Flag Army and Qing China

battles.name: Battle of Alapan
battles.summary: Filipino revolutionaries under Emilio Aguinaldo beat a Spanish garrison at Alapan in Imus, Cavite. The Philippine flag is said to have flown in battle there for the first time.

battles.name: Capture of Trincomalee
battles.summary: A British force took the Dutch fort and harbour of Trincomalee in Ceylon in the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War. The French took it later that same year.

battles.name: Battle of Abancay
battles.summary: In the civil war between Spanish conquerors in Peru, Diego de Almagro's men beat the Pizarro brothers' army on the Abancay river.
sides: Pizarro army under Alonso de Alvarado

battles.name: Battle of Tlatelolco
battles.summary: The Mexica of Tenochtitlan conquered their twin city Tlatelolco. Its ruler Moquihuix died and Tlatelolco lost its independence.

battles.name: Battle of Tocarema
battles.summary: Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada's conquistadors, fighting alongside Muisca warriors, beat the Panche people west of Bogotá.

battles.name: Battle of Quiapo
battles.summary: In the Arauco War, Spanish troops stormed a Mapuche fort at Quiapo in southern Chile.

battles.name: Battle of Sangarará
battles.summary: The first big victory of Túpac Amaru II's uprising in Peru: his army destroyed a colonial force sent out from Cusco.

battles.name: Great Swamp Fight
battles.summary: In King Philip's War, colonial militia attacked a fortified Narragansett village in a frozen swamp in Rhode Island, killing hundreds of people, many of them women and children.

battles.name: Battle of Bloody Marsh
battles.summary: On St Simons Island, British and colonial troops ambushed a Spanish force in the War of Jenkins' Ear; Spain soon gave up its invasion of Georgia.

battles.name: Battle of Bushy Run
battles.summary: During Pontiac's War, Henry Bouquet's column beat off a two-day attack by Native American warriors and went on to relieve Fort Pitt.
sides: Delaware, Shawnee, Mingo and Wyandot warriors

battles.name: Battle of Grand Pré
battles.summary: In a winter raid during King George's War, French, Mi'kmaq and Acadian fighters surprised New England troops sleeping in houses at Grand-Pré, Nova Scotia.
sides: New France with Mi'kmaq and Acadian allies

battles.name: Battle of Rio de Janeiro (1710)
battles.summary: A French raid under Jean-François Duclerc was beaten in the streets of Rio de Janeiro and Duclerc was captured. A second French fleet took the city the next year.

battles.name: Second Battle of Salvador da Bahia
battles.wikiTitle: Second Battle of Salvador da Bahia
battles.summary: John Maurice of Nassau's Dutch army besieged Salvador da Bahia, capital of Portuguese Brazil, but failed to take it.
battles.dateNote: Wikidata gives the month only: April 1638.

battles.name: Battle of Santo Domingo (1586)
battles.summary: Francis Drake's raiders took the Spanish colonial capital of Santo Domingo and held it for ransom for about a month.

battles.name: Battle for Río San Juan de Nicaragua
battles.wikiTitle: Battle for Río San Juan de Nicaragua
battles.summary: The Spanish fort on the San Juan river in Nicaragua held off a British attack. The defence is linked with Rafaela Herrera, who is said to have led it as a teenager.

battles.name: Battle of Kepaniwai
battles.summary: Kamehameha's army beat the forces of Maui in the ʻĪao Valley. Tradition says so many died that the stream was dammed with bodies, which gave the battle its name.

battles.name: Battle of Mokuʻōhai
battles.summary: Kamehameha defeated his cousin Kīwalaʻō, who was killed. It began Kamehameha's rise to rule all the Hawaiian Islands.
battles.dateNote: Wikidata gives the month only: July 1782.

battles.name: Battle of Nuʻuanu
battles.summary: Kamehameha's army drove the Oʻahu forces up the Nuʻuanu Valley to the Pali cliffs, uniting most of the Hawaiian Islands under his rule.
battles.dateNote: Wikidata gives the month only: May 1795.

battles.name: Battle of Ōhaeawai
battles.summary: In the Flagstaff War, British troops stormed the Māori pā (fort) at Ōhaeawai and were driven back with heavy losses.
sides: Ngāpuhi under Hōne Heke and Te Ruki Kawiti
battles.dateNote: Wikidata gives the month only: July 1845.

battles.name: Castle Hill convict rebellion
battles.summary: Hundreds of convicts, most of them Irish, rose near Castle Hill in New South Wales. Soldiers crushed them at Rouse Hill, a fight also called the second Battle of Vinegar Hill.

battles.name: Battle of Isurava
battles.summary: On the Kokoda Track, Australian troops held off a much larger Japanese force for several days before falling back.
battles.result: Japanese victory; the Australians fell back in good order

battles.name: Battle of Kaiapit
battles.summary: Australian commandos flown into the Markham Valley took the village of Kaiapit from a larger Japanese force.

people.name: Ogino Ginko
people.summary: The first woman licensed to practise Western medicine in Japan.
people.placeNote: Shown at Kumagaya, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Tsuda Umeko
people.summary: A pioneer of women's education in Japan. She founded the school that became Tsuda University.
people.placeNote: Shown at Minamichō, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Isabella I of Castile
people.summary: Queen of Castile. Her marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon joined the crowns of Spain, and she backed Columbus's voyage of 1492.
people.placeNote: Shown at Monasterio de Nuestra Señora de Gracia, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Dorothy Hodgkin
people.summary: British chemist who worked out the structures of penicillin, vitamin B12 and insulin using X-rays. Nobel Prize in Chemistry, 1964.
people.placeNote: Shown at Cairo, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Tu Youyou
people.summary: Chinese scientist who discovered artemisinin, a malaria medicine that has saved millions of lives. Nobel Prize in Medicine, 2015.
people.placeNote: Shown at Ningbo, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Chiquinha Gonzaga
people.summary: Brazilian composer and pianist, often named as the first woman to conduct an orchestra in Brazil.
people.placeNote: Shown at Rio de Janeiro, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Rosalind Franklin
people.summary: Her X-ray photographs of DNA were key evidence for its double-helix shape.
people.placeNote: Shown at Notting Hill, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Truganini
people.summary: A Palawa (Aboriginal Tasmanian) woman who lived through the British invasion of Tasmania. She became a symbol of survival and of the wrongs done to her people.
people.placeNote: Shown at Bruny Island, where Wikidata records the birth.
people.dateNote: Wikidata gives the year only, and it is an estimate: about 1812.

people.name: Albert Namatjira
people.summary: Western Arrernte painter, famous for his watercolour landscapes of Central Australia.
people.placeNote: Shown at Hermannsburg, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Juana Azurduy de Padilla
people.summary: Guerrilla leader in the wars of independence of Upper Peru, today Bolivia.
people.placeNote: Shown at Sucre, where Wikidata records the birth.
people.dateNote: Wikidata gives the month only: July 1780.

people.name: Gabriela Silang
people.summary: Led the Ilocano revolt against Spanish rule after her husband Diego Silang was killed.
people.placeNote: Shown at Santa, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf
people.summary: President of Liberia from 2006 to 2018, the first elected woman head of state in Africa. Nobel Peace Prize, 2011.
people.placeNote: Shown at Monrovia, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Kartini
people.summary: Javanese writer whose letters argued for girls' schooling and women's rights. She is a national heroine of Indonesia.
people.placeNote: Shown at Jepara, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Dewi Sartika
people.summary: Opened one of the first schools for girls in the Dutch East Indies, in Bandung in 1904.
people.placeNote: Shown at Cicalengka, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: C. V. Raman
people.summary: Physicist who discovered the Raman effect, a change in light scattered by molecules. Nobel Prize in Physics, 1930.
people.placeNote: Shown at Tiruchirappalli, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Kalpana Chawla
people.summary: The first woman of Indian origin to fly in space. She died in the Columbia shuttle disaster in 2003.
people.placeNote: Shown at Karnal, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Homi J. Bhabha
people.summary: Physicist who founded India's nuclear research programme.
people.placeNote: Shown at Mumbai, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Policarpa Salavarrieta
people.summary: A spy for the independence fighters in New Granada (Colombia). She was executed by the Spanish and became a national heroine.
people.placeNote: Shown at Guaduas, where Wikidata records the birth.
people.dateNote: Her birth date is not certain; Wikidata gives 26 January 1795.

people.name: Rigoberta Menchú
people.summary: Kʼicheʼ Maya campaigner for Indigenous people's rights in Guatemala. Nobel Peace Prize, 1992.
people.placeNote: Shown at Laj Chimel, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Queen Emma of Hawaii
people.summary: Queen of Kamehameha IV. She helped found The Queen's Hospital in Honolulu.
people.placeNote: Shown at Honolulu, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Mumtaz Mahal
people.summary: Mughal empress. After her death Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as her tomb.
people.placeNote: Shown at Agra, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Cuauhtémoc
people.summary: The last Aztec emperor, who led the defence of Tenochtitlan against the Spanish in 1521.
people.placeNote: Shown at Tenochtitlan, where Wikidata records the birth.
people.dateNote: Wikidata gives the year only, and it is an estimate: about 1495.

people.name: Leona Vicario
people.summary: Supporter and journalist of Mexican independence, honoured as a heroine of the nation.
people.placeNote: Shown at Mexico City, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Nur Jahan
people.summary: Mughal empress, wife of Jahangir. She held real power at court and had coins struck in her own name.
people.placeNote: Shown at Kandahar, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Zumbi dos Palmares
people.summary: The last leader of Palmares, a large settlement of people who escaped slavery in Brazil. Brazil's Black Consciousness Day is held on the day he died.
people.placeNote: Shown at Palmares, where Wikidata records the birth.
people.dateNote: Wikidata gives the year only, and it is an estimate: about 1655.

people.name: Yu Gwan-sun
people.summary: A teenage organiser of the 1919 March First Movement for Korean independence. She died in a Japanese prison.
people.placeNote: Shown at Cheonan, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Antonio Maceo
people.summary: General in Cuba's wars of independence from Spain, known as the 'Bronze Titan'.
people.placeNote: Shown at San Luis, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Mariana Grajales Cuello
people.summary: Mother of Antonio Maceo. Cuba honours her as a 'Mother of the Nation' for her part in the independence wars.
people.placeNote: Shown at Santiago de Cuba, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Rani Lakshmibai
people.summary: Rani of Jhansi. She led her troops against the British in the 1857 uprising and died fighting.
people.placeNote: Shown at Varanasi, where Wikidata records the birth.
people.dateNote: Wikidata gives 19 November 1828; some sources give 1835 instead.

people.name: Janaki Ammal
people.summary: Botanist who bred sweeter sugarcane and studied plant chromosomes; one of the first Indian women to earn a doctorate in botany.
people.placeNote: Shown at Thalassery, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Micaela Bastidas
people.summary: Wife and fellow leader of Túpac Amaru II in the great rebellion in Peru. She was executed in Cusco in 1781.
people.placeNote: Shown at Tamburco District, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Bayinnaung
people.summary: King of the Toungoo dynasty who built one of the largest empires in the history of Southeast Asia.
people.placeNote: Shown at Taungoo, where Wikidata records the birth.

people.name: Teresa Magbanua
people.summary: A school teacher who led troops in the Philippine Revolution, called the 'Visayan Joan of Arc'.
people.placeNote: Shown at Pototan, where Wikidata records the birth.

discoveries.name: Lomekwi 3 stone tools
discoveries.summary: Stone tools about 3.3 million years old, found west of Lake Turkana. They are older than any known Homo fossil, so they may have been made by an earlier human relative.
discoveries.dateNote: Found in 2011; published in Nature in 2015 (Harmand et al.).

discoveries.name: Kalambo Falls wooden structure
discoveries.summary: Two logs joined by a cut notch, about 476,000 years old. They may be the oldest known wooden structure built by human relatives.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in Nature in 2023 (Barham et al.).

discoveries.name: Jebel Irhoud fossils redated
discoveries.summary: New finds and dating put these fossils at about 300,000 years old, the oldest widely accepted remains of Homo sapiens.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in Nature in 2017 (Hublin et al.). The site itself was first dug in the 1960s.

discoveries.name: Homo luzonensis
discoveries.summary: Teeth and bones from Callao Cave on Luzon were named as a new human species, at least 50,000 years old.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in Nature in 2019 (Détroit et al.).

discoveries.name: Toumaï skull (Sahelanthropus)
discoveries.summary: A skull about 7 million years old from the Djurab Desert. It may be one of the earliest members of the human family, though whether it walked upright is still debated.
discoveries.dateNote: Found in 2001; published in Nature in 2002 (Brunet et al.).

discoveries.name: Laetoli footprints
discoveries.summary: A trail of footprints left in volcanic ash about 3.6 million years ago, showing that early human relatives walked upright.
discoveries.dateNote: Found in 1978; published in Nature in 1979 (Leakey and Hay).

discoveries.name: Denisovans identified
discoveries.summary: DNA from a tiny finger bone found in Denisova Cave revealed a human group no one had known about, now called the Denisovans.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in Nature in 2010 (Krause et al.).

discoveries.name: Pinnacle Point cave finds
discoveries.summary: Shellfish meals and red ochre pigment about 164,000 years old, among the earliest signs of people living off the sea.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in Nature in 2007 (Marean et al.).

discoveries.name: Diepkloof engraved eggshells
discoveries.summary: Ostrich eggshell water containers engraved with patterns about 60,000 years ago, an early example of symbols.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in PNAS in 2010 (Texier et al.).

discoveries.name: Mata Menge fossils
discoveries.summary: A jaw and teeth about 700,000 years old from Flores. They are probably early relatives of the small "hobbit" people, Homo floresiensis.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in Nature in 2016 (van den Bergh et al.).

discoveries.name: White Sands footprints
discoveries.summary: Human footprints dated to about 21,000 to 23,000 years ago, which may mean people reached the Americas during the last Ice Age. The dates were questioned, and a 2023 study supported them.
discoveries.dateNote: Published in Science in 2021 (Bennett et al.). Shown at the national park, where the footprints are.

states.name: Kingdom of Aksum
states.dateNote: Both dates are rough; Wikidata gives about 400 BC and about 960 AD.
